surface: A commented cell and the comment editor opened from the keyboard: its name, typing into it, saving with Ctrl+Enter, closing with Escape, and the grid's keys after it closes.

steps.note: B1, a cell without a comment, before the commented one. The setup gives both comments texts without the word `comment`, so the comment group of the later steps passes only on a reader that names the comment, never on its text. NVDA spells a cell value such as `B1` as `B 1`. Finding: VoiceOver with WebKit says nothing on this first arrow key.

B2 carries a comment. The grid draws it as a corner mark (the `htCommentCell` class) with nothing in the accessibility tree, so a reader should say the cell has a comment before a user opens it. Finding: no reader says the cell has a comment; all four read B2 as a plain cell.

Ctrl+Alt+M opens the comment editor on the selected cell and focuses its text field: the comment's text, the field's editable role (NVDA `edit, multi line`, VoiceOver `text entry area`) and its name, which says the field is a comment. Finding: no reader names the field; it has no accessible name (the axe baseline's `editor-input-names`), so a user hears an unnamed text field holding the comment.

Text typed at the end of the comment. Nothing is required: a reader's echo of typed keys is its own setting, not the grid's (VoiceOver with WebKit echoes `Ana .`, the others say nothing). The reopen step proves the text was taken.

Ctrl+Enter (Cmd+Enter on macOS) closes the editor and saves the comment, and the focus should return to the commented cell. Finding: the focus lands on the document body (a local probe: `document.activeElement` is `body` while the grid still listens, and the next arrow key brings the focus back to a cell). NVDA reads the document (`Handsontable e2e fixture — comment editor resize, document`), VoiceOver with Chromium says `group`, and VoiceOver with WebKit says nothing.

Ctrl+Alt+M again: the editor holds the saved comment, the typed text included. NVDA reads only the line at the caret of a multi-line field, and the narrow editor wraps the comment so that its last line is `Ana.`: `ana` is the same fact in NVDA's reading. VoiceOver reads the whole comment.

Escape closes the editor without saving, and the focus should return to the commented cell. Finding: as after Ctrl+Enter, the focus lands on the document body; NVDA reads the document, VoiceOver with Chromium says `group`, and VoiceOver with WebKit says nothing.
The grid answers the arrow keys after the editor closed: every reader reads B3, NVDA and VoiceOver after announcing the table again.
A4, the second commented cell, reached after the editor closed. Finding: as on B2, no reader says the cell has a comment.
